units.english: agent_0 agrees to the current agent being finished by the person associated with speaking and the whole group.
notes: The prompt uses descriptive groups rather than bound proper-name handles. [PERSON/AGENT SAY GROUP ALL] has intersecting modifiers and no marked “speaks for” relation. “The person associated with speaking and the whole group” is a cautious referring description, not a named person or a verified title.

[PERSON/AGENT ITEM NOW] denotes the current agent/item. [PERSON/AGENT ITEM FUTURE GOOD], when present, denotes a future beneficial agent/item. These descriptions do not themselves encode AI, a particular name, improved capability, or matching goals.

The nested predicate is FINISH/COMPLETE, not a lexical verb for killing, deactivating, or replacing. With an agent/item as theme, precisely what completion entails is unspecified; the English retains the unusual object. The clause asserts agreement with that event, not its actual completion.
evidence: Both clauses use SUN: 𗞚 = agree/accept; 𗉶 = finish/complete. The nested subject is [PERSON/AGENT SAY GROUP ALL] and its theme is [PERSON/AGENT ITEM NOW].
